title: Arm-wrestling style preacher curls tutorial
summary: NH demonstrates a single-arm preacher curl taught to him by a French arm wrestler: a supramaximal one-arm negative stopped at about 45 degrees, with the other hand assisting the positive. He covers safety, wrist supination for forearm involvement, and programming it for 3-7 reps over 3-4 sets.
claims: This preacher curl variation is not for novices; if you are not comfortable with biceps training it carries injury risk from uncontrolled range of motion
The lift lets people who already have good biceps overload them safely and rack up a lot of quality tonnage quickly
He learned it from a French arm wrestler, has done it every 10 days for a year, and is still progressing
Stop the negative at about 45 degrees, before the biceps overextends; with heavy weight never go to full extension because an overstretched tendon under load is a recipe for injury
Because you are stronger eccentrically, you can lower supramaximal weight with one arm and use the other hand to help bring it back up
Keep the free hand underneath the working arm during the negative, without helping, so it can catch the weight if something goes wrong
Stop the positive when the forearm is perpendicular to the floor; curling further only adds a squeeze that is not worth it
When finishing near failure, pull the dumbbell close to your body to shorten the moment arm and rest it on the pad; never stand up with it or drop it
To involve more forearm, rotate the wrist inward as you lower, then tilt it back as you come up so the handle stays in the palm and does not roll
He programs it for 3-7 reps over 3-4 sets
Mechanical failure plays a role: once your ability to supinate the wrist fails, the curl is gone
Start with the weight you can curl strictly on the preacher; every overloading movement should be introduced safely and in a controlled setting
The tryout period teaches you the right angle and grip and whether the lift suits you, since not every lift suits everyone
exercises: slow one-arm negative to about 45 degrees; free hand underneath for safety; other hand assists positive; supinate wrist going down, tilt back coming up; bring dumbbell close to body to finish
supramaximal eccentric overload for biceps and inner forearm
